title: Driving at Night & Dazzle
whatItIs: At night you see less and others see you less. Use your lights well and never dazzle other road users.
keyFacts: If oncoming headlights dazzle you, slow down and stop if you need to.
Dip your headlights for oncoming traffic and when you are following another vehicle.
When overtaking at night, stay on dipped beam until you are level, then use main beam if needed.
Drive at a speed that lets you stop within the distance your lights show to be clear.
Pedestrians, cyclists and horse riders are much harder to see after dark.

visual.caption: Seeing and being seen at night

items.title: Main beam
items.text: On unlit roads when nobody is ahead or coming towards you.

items.title: Dipped beam
items.text: In built-up areas, for oncoming traffic and when following.

items.title: Dazzled
items.text: Slow down, and stop if you need to. Don't look at the lights.

items.title: Clean glass
items.text: A dirty windscreen makes glare much worse at night.

onTheTest.question: You are dazzled by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle. What should you do?
options: Slow down, and stop if you need to
onTheTest.why: If you are dazzled, slow down and if necessary stop until you can see properly again.

traps: Don't answer dazzle with your own main beam.
At dusk, cyclists and pedestrians are especially hard to see.
Tiredness is worse at night: plan rest breaks.
